effects.text: At the level of the lesion: a band of all-modality sensory loss and flaccid weakness in the damaged segments (dorsal horn, root and ventral horn).

sites.name: Central cord lesion (syrinx): anterior white commissure

effects.text: Dissociated sensory loss: pain and temperature lost in a 'cape' over the shoulders and arms (the damaged cervical segments); vibration and position sense preserved (the dorsal columns are spared).
Dissociated sensory loss: pain and temperature lost in a band over the damaged thoracic segments; vibration and position sense preserved (the dorsal columns are spared).

sites.name: Anterior spinal artery territory (anterior two thirds of the cord)

effects.text: Dorsal columns spared (vibration and position sense intact): they are supplied by the posterior spinal arteries.

sites.name: Posterior spinal artery (dorsal column and dorsal horn, one side)

effects.text: At the damaged segments the dorsal horn is lost too: a band of sensory loss on that side. Below the lesion, strength and pain/temperature are largely preserved (anterior spinal artery territory).
At the damaged segments the dorsal horns are lost too: a band of sensory loss. Below the lesion, strength and pain/temperature are largely preserved (anterior spinal artery territory).

sites.name: Ventral horn / ventral root (lower motor neuron)
Medial medullary lesion (pyramid, medial lemniscus, hypoglossal)

effects.text: Hypoglossal nucleus or fascicles: the tongue deviates toward the lesion (lower motor neuron, same side).
The face is spared: the corticobulbar fibres leave the corticospinal bundle above the medulla.
Nucleus ambiguus: hoarseness, dysphagia, the palate and uvula pulled away from the lesion.
Descending sympathetic fibres: Horner syndrome (ptosis, miosis, anhidrosis).
Vestibular nuclei: vertigo, nystagmus.
Awake and aware, but quadriplegic with only vertical eye movements and blinking preserved (the reticular activating system and vertical gaze centres lie above the lesion).

sites.name: Principal sensory nucleus of V (rostral pons)

effects.text: If the oculomotor fascicles are included (Weber syndrome): dilated pupil, eye turned down and out, ptosis on the lesion side.

sites.name: Midbrain tegmentum (medial lemniscus, spinothalamic tract, red nucleus)
Decussation of the superior cerebellar peduncle
Posterior limb of the internal capsule
Internal capsule (genu and posterior limb), e.g. a capsular stroke

effects.text: Contralateral superior quadrantanopia (pie in the sky): Meyer's loop carries the upper visual field.

sites.name: Optic radiation, parietal route (dorsal fibres: lower field)

effects.text: Contralateral inferior quadrantanopia: the parietal route carries the lower visual field.
Macular (central) sparing is typical of a posterior cerebral artery stroke (dual blood supply of the occipital pole).
Ipsilateral intention tremor, dysmetria, dysdiadochokinesia and a wide-based gait: the cerebellum acts on the same side because its output crosses once and the descending tract crosses back.
Loss of the corneal reflex's afferent limb: no blink in either eye on touching this cornea.
Hemiballismus: sudden, violent flinging movements of the opposite arm and leg (loss of the indirect pathway's drive on GPi).
Parkinsonism: resting tremor, rigidity, bradykinesia, shuffling gait (dopamine lost, so the direct pathway is under-driven and the indirect over-driven). Usually bilateral, asymmetric.
Huntington disease: chorea and dementia (loss of striatal output neurons, GABAergic, so the indirect pathway is lost).
Anterograde amnesia: cannot form new memories, old memories recalled (bilateral damage).
Blunted fear responses (bilateral damage).
